Moreover, a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a manner similar to what we have said has been transmitted.

Mention of the report transmitted to that effect:
- Narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said: Narrated to us Abbad ibn Rashid, from Qatadah, who said: Khulayd al-Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which the sun sets but that two angels stand beside it, calling out, which all of Allah's creatures hear except the two jinn and humans: 'O Allah, give the spender a replacement, and give the withholder destruction.'" So Allah revealed in that regard the Qur'an: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best﴾ ... to His words ﴿toward hardship﴾.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to me Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq used to free slaves for Islam in Mecca. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: "My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only you freed strong men who would stand with you, protect you, and defend you." He said: "My father, I only want what is with Allah." He said: "One of my household told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾:

He says: We will prepare him for the easy path, which is acting in the way that Allah is pleased with in this world, so that by it He will make Paradise necessary for him in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for him who withholds spending in the way of Allah and refrains from what Allah has bestowed upon him of His bounty, not spending it in the ways Allah commanded, and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord, so that he does not desire to Him by working in His obedience and increasing what He has entrusted to him of that.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with what he has and considers himself self-sufficient within himself."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "and as for him who is stingy with the bounty and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: Narrated to me my father, who said: Narrated to me my paternal uncle, who said: Narrated to me my father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: "He whom Allah has made wealthy, yet he withholds the zakat."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with the right of Allah over him and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."

As for His words ﴿and denies the best﴾, the exegetes differed about its interpretation, similar to their difference regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾. As for us, we say: its meaning is: "and denies the replacement."

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "and denies the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "with the replacement from Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies the promise of Allah that He made." Allah said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And the disbeliever denies Allah's good promise."

Others said: Its meaning is: "And denies the oneness of Allah" (tawhid, the affirmation of God's unity).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies: There is no god but Allah."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "There is no god but Allah."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And denies Paradise."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾, he said: "[It means] Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾:

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "We will prepare him in this world for the hard state." It derives from their saying: qad yasarat ghanam fulan (the sheep of so-and-so have "become easy"), meaning when they gave birth and were prepared for birthing. As the poet said:

They claim to be our lords, but they only rule over us
Because their two flocks gave birth with ease.

[The verb irtafa'a al-amr (ارتفع الأمر) means: it ceased and went away, as if it had been placed present and then lifted. From it: irtafa'a al-khilaf baynahuma (the dispute between them was removed).]

It was also said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ is not an ease in hardship, because of what came earlier in the beginning of the passage in His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾. When two statements are combined, one mentioning good and the other mentioning evil, it is permissible for ease to apply to both together. The "hardship" that Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed us He will ease him toward is: doing what He dislikes and does not approve of.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agrees with what we have said about this.

Mention of the report with that:

⁕ Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he scratched the ground, then raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and his seat in the Fire have been written." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy [for what he was created for]." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Za'ida ibn Qudama narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were at a funeral in al-Baqi', when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us and sat, and we sat with him. He had a stick with which he scratched the ground, then he raised his head to the sky and said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that its entrance has been written." The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on our Book? Whoever is among the people of happiness will act for happiness, and whoever is among the people of misery will act for misery." He said: "Rather, act, for each is made easy; as for he who is of the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the works of happiness, and as for he who is of the people of misery, he will be made easy for misery." Then he recited: (﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾).

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, that they both heard Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was at a funeral, took a stick, and began scratching the ground. He said: "There is none but that his seat in the Fire or in Paradise has been written." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy. ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), when he took something from the ground with his hand and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and in the Fire is known." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah]﴾ ... the two verses.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Samura ibn Abi Za'ida, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabra, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that Allah has written for it what it will encounter." A Bedouin was with the Prophet (ﷺ), seeking [guidance], and the Bedouin said: "Then what brought me, to strike from the valley of such-and-such, if the matter has already been finished?"

So the Prophet (ﷺ) scratched the ground until the people thought he wished he had not spoken any of it. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for. Whoever Allah wishes good for, He makes easy for the path of good, and whoever He wishes evil for, He makes easy for the path of evil." I met Amr ibn Murra and presented this hadith to him, and he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said [it]," and he added in it: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created by [divine] decree﴾, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of action? Is it in something we will begin, or in something that has already been finished?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Act, for each is made easy: We will ease him toward ease, and We will ease him toward hardship."

⁕ Amr ibn Abd al-Malik al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayda narrated to us, saying: al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artat, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who raised the report to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting one day with a stick in his hand, scratching the ground with it. He raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise or in the Fire is known." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely [on that]?" He said to them: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he said: "Have you not heard Allah in His Book saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾?"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾: "[It means] toward evil from Allah."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act for a matter that has been finished, or for a matter we are beginning?" He (ﷺ) said: "Every doer is made easy for his deed."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Talq ibn Habib, from Bashir ibn Ka'b, who said: Two young men asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act in accordance with what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon, or in something that is being newly begun?" He said: "Rather, in what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" He said: "Act, for each doer is made easy for the deed for which he was created." They said: "Then now we will strive and act."

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿By the night when it covers (1), and by the day when it appears in brightness (2), and by Him who created the male and the female (3), indeed your effort is diverse (4). As for him who gives and fears Allah (5), and affirms the best (6), We will ease him toward ease (7). But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient (8), and denies the best (9), We will ease him toward hardship (10).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, swearing by the night when it covers the day with its darkness, extinguishing its light and bringing its gloom: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ the day ﴿and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾. This is also an oath: He swears by the day when it shines, gives light, and becomes visible to the eyes, after the darkness of night had come between them and seeing it directly. Qatadah held that when Allah swears by things, He only swears by them because of their great standing with Him.

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the night when it covers and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾: "Two great signs which Allah folds over the creatures."

* *

As for His words ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾:

This may bear the two meanings I described in His words ﴿by the heaven and He who built it﴾ and ﴿by the earth and He who spread it out﴾. Namely, one may take "mā" to mean "man" (who), so that it is an oath by the Creator of the male and the female, namely that Creator Himself; or one may take "mā" together with what follows it to mean a verbal noun (maṣdar), so that it is an oath by His creating the male and the female.

It has been reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda' that they used to recite it as ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾ (and the male and the female). Abu al-Darda' transmitted this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: In the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): ﴿and the night when it covers, and the day when it appears in brightness, and the male and the female﴾.
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik [[That is, a poor statement. See above p. 165, no. 1.]], who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, who said: Al-Mughirah informed me, who said: I heard Ibrahim say: Alqamah came to Syria and sat down with Abu al-Darda'. He said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "These people kept at it until they nearly led me astray, yet I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Hatim ibn Wardan, who said: Narrated to us Abu Hamzah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: We came to Syria, and I entered upon Abu al-Darda'. He questioned me and said: "How did you hear Ibn Mas'ud recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "That is enough. I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting it thus."
- Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Ulayyah; and Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti narrated to me, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, who said: I arrived in Syria and met Abu al-Darda', who said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Iraq." He said: "From which part?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "Do you recite it in the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Recite ﴿and the night when it covers﴾." So I recited: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾. He laughed, then said: "That is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to me Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to me Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording.
- Narrated to me Abu al-Sa'ib, who said: Narrated to us Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: I came to Syria, and Abu al-Darda' came and said: "Is there anyone among you who can recite to me in the recitation of Abdullah?" They pointed to me. I said: "I can." He said: "How did you hear Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾?" I said: "That is how I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." He said: "These people want me to recite ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾, but I will not follow them."
- Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾. He said: "In some readings it is ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, the same.
- Narrated to me Ahmad ibn Yusuf, who said: Narrated to us al-Qasim, who said: Narrated to us Hajjaj, from Harun, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan, that he used to recite it ﴿wa-mā khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā﴾, saying: "Wa-lladhī khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā" (and He who created the male and the female). Harun said: Abu Amr said: "The people of Mecca say to thunder: 'Glory be to what you glorify.'"
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Jarir, from Mughirah, from Miqsam al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Abi Imran, from Alqamah ibn Qays Abu Shibl: that he came to Syria, entered the mosque, prayed in it, then went to a circle and sat in it. He said: "A man came to me. I recognized in him the way the people gave way to him and stood in awe of him. He sat beside me, so I said: 'Praise be to Allah, I truly hope that Allah has answered my supplication.' That man was Abu al-Darda'. He said: 'What is that?' Alqamah said: 'I asked Allah to grant me a righteous companion, and I hope that you are he.' He said: 'Where are you from?' I said: 'From Kufa,' or 'from the people of Iraq, from Kufa.' Abu al-Darda' said: 'Was there not among you the owner of the two sandals, the cushion and the water vessel,' meaning Ibn Mas'ud? 'Or was there not among you one whom Allah protected from the accursed Satan through the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ),' meaning Ammar ibn Yasir? 'Or was there not among you the keeper of the secret which no one else knows,' or someone other than him, meaning Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman?' Then he said: 'Which of you can memorize as Abdullah used to recite?' I said: 'I can.' He said: 'Recite: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾.' Alqamah said: So I recited ﴿al-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾. Abu al-Darda' said: 'By Him besides whom there is no god, this is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to me, from his mouth to mine.' These people kept at it until they nearly made me give it up."

* *

As for His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾:

He says: Indeed your deeds are diverse, O people, for among you is the unbeliever in his Lord, the one who disobeys Him in His commands and prohibitions, and the believer in Him, the one who obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions.

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾: "It means: different."

* *

As for His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾:

This is the answer to the oath. The meaning is: "By the night when it covers, indeed your effort is diverse." The scholars also said so.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: "The oath concludes here with ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿As for him who gives﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for him who gives and fears Allah among you, O people, in the way of Allah, and whom Allah has commanded to give from his wealth, and what He has bestowed upon him of His bounty, and fears Allah and avoids His prohibitions.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Amir, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾: "He gives what he has and fears Allah." He said: "He fears his Lord."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿As for him who gives﴾ from the bounty ﴿and fears﴾: "He fears his Lord."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿As for him who gives﴾: "the right of Allah," ﴿and fears﴾: "the prohibitions of Allah which He forbade."
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Narrated to us Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾: "He is the one who remembers Allah and fears Allah."

The exegetes differed about the interpretation of His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "and affirms the replacement from Allah for what he gave from his wealth in the matters in which Allah commanded him to give."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to me Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "and affirms the replacement from Allah."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to me Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "He affirms the replacement from Allah."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Ulayyah, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, the same.
- Narrated to us Isma'il ibn Musa al-Suddi, who said: Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-Ahmasi informed us, from Sa'id ibn al-Salt, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "He is certain of the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "that Allah will replace it for him."
- He said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Abu Hashim al-Makki, from Mujahid: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, who said: "with the replacement."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "and affirms that Allah is One, with no partner."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali al-Muqaddami, who said: Narrated to us Ash'ath al-Sijistani, who said: Narrated to us Mis'ar; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Mis'ar, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "There is no god but Allah."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, the same.
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, the same.
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Narrated to us Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "There is no god but Allah."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: Narrated to me my father, who said: Narrated to me my paternal uncle, who said: Narrated to me my father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "He affirms 'There is no god but Allah.'"

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "and affirms Paradise."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "Paradise."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Muhabbab, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "and affirms the promise of Allah."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "the promise of Allah for Himself, so he acts on that promise which Allah promised."
- Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "The believer affirms the good promise of Allah."

The sayings most similar to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates, and most correct in my view, are: the saying of the one who said that it refers to affirming the replacement from Allah for his spending.

I only said that this is the most correct of the sayings because Allah mentioned before it a spender who spent, seeking from his spending a replacement for it. So the most fitting meaning is that what follows it be a report of his affirming the promise of Allah to him of a replacement, since his spending was in the manner that pleases Him. Moreover, a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a manner similar to what we have said has been transmitted.

Mention of the report transmitted to that effect:
- Narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said: Narrated to us Abbad ibn Rashid, from Qatadah, who said: Khulayd al-Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which the sun sets but that two angels stand beside it, calling out, which all of Allah's creatures hear except the two jinn and humans: 'O Allah, give the spender a replacement, and give the withholder destruction.'" So Allah revealed in that regard the Qur'an: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best﴾ ... to His words ﴿toward hardship﴾.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to me Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq used to free slaves for Islam in Mecca. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: "My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only you freed strong men who would stand with you, protect you, and defend you." He said: "My father, I only want what is with Allah." He said: "One of my household told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾:

He says: We will prepare him for the easy path, which is acting in the way that Allah is pleased with in this world, so that by it He will make Paradise necessary for him in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for him who withholds spending in the way of Allah and refrains from what Allah has bestowed upon him of His bounty, not spending it in the ways Allah commanded, and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord, so that he does not desire to Him by working in His obedience and increasing what He has entrusted to him of that.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with what he has and considers himself self-sufficient within himself."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "and as for him who is stingy with the bounty and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: Narrated to me my father, who said: Narrated to me my paternal uncle, who said: Narrated to me my father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: "He whom Allah has made wealthy, yet he withholds the zakat."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with the right of Allah over him and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."

As for His words ﴿and denies the best﴾, the exegetes differed about its interpretation, similar to their difference regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾. As for us, we say: its meaning is: "and denies the replacement."

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "and denies the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "with the replacement from Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies the promise of Allah that He made." Allah said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And the disbeliever denies Allah's good promise."

Others said: Its meaning is: "And denies the oneness of Allah" (tawhid, the affirmation of God's unity).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies: There is no god but Allah."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "There is no god but Allah."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And denies Paradise."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾, he said: "[It means] Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾:

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "We will prepare him in this world for the hard state." It derives from their saying: qad yasarat ghanam fulan (the sheep of so-and-so have "become easy"), meaning when they gave birth and were prepared for birthing. As the poet said:

They claim to be our lords, but they only rule over us
Because their two flocks gave birth with ease.

[The verb irtafa'a al-amr (ارتفع الأمر) means: it ceased and went away, as if it had been placed present and then lifted. From it: irtafa'a al-khilaf baynahuma (the dispute between them was removed).]

It was also said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ is not an ease in hardship, because of what came earlier in the beginning of the passage in His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾. When two statements are combined, one mentioning good and the other mentioning evil, it is permissible for ease to apply to both together. The "hardship" that Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed us He will ease him toward is: doing what He dislikes and does not approve of.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agrees with what we have said about this.

Mention of the report with that:

⁕ Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he scratched the ground, then raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and his seat in the Fire have been written." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy [for what he was created for]." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Za'ida ibn Qudama narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were at a funeral in al-Baqi', when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us and sat, and we sat with him. He had a stick with which he scratched the ground, then he raised his head to the sky and said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that its entrance has been written." The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on our Book? Whoever is among the people of happiness will act for happiness, and whoever is among the people of misery will act for misery." He said: "Rather, act, for each is made easy; as for he who is of the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the works of happiness, and as for he who is of the people of misery, he will be made easy for misery." Then he recited: (﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾).

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, that they both heard Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was at a funeral, took a stick, and began scratching the ground. He said: "There is none but that his seat in the Fire or in Paradise has been written." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy. ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), when he took something from the ground with his hand and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and in the Fire is known." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah]﴾ ... the two verses.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Samura ibn Abi Za'ida, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabra, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that Allah has written for it what it will encounter." A Bedouin was with the Prophet (ﷺ), seeking [guidance], and the Bedouin said: "Then what brought me, to strike from the valley of such-and-such, if the matter has already been finished?"

So the Prophet (ﷺ) scratched the ground until the people thought he wished he had not spoken any of it. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for. Whoever Allah wishes good for, He makes easy for the path of good, and whoever He wishes evil for, He makes easy for the path of evil." I met Amr ibn Murra and presented this hadith to him, and he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said [it]," and he added in it: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created by [divine] decree﴾, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of action? Is it in something we will begin, or in something that has already been finished?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Act, for each is made easy: We will ease him toward ease, and We will ease him toward hardship."

⁕ Amr ibn Abd al-Malik al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayda narrated to us, saying: al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artat, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who raised the report to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting one day with a stick in his hand, scratching the ground with it. He raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise or in the Fire is known." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely [on that]?" He said to them: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he said: "Have you not heard Allah in His Book saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾?"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾: "[It means] toward evil from Allah."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act for a matter that has been finished, or for a matter we are beginning?" He (ﷺ) said: "Every doer is made easy for his deed."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Talq ibn Habib, from Bashir ibn Ka'b, who said: Two young men asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act in accordance with what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon, or in something that is being newly begun?" He said: "Rather, in what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" He said: "Act, for each doer is made easy for the deed for which he was created." They said: "Then now we will strive and act."

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿By the night when it covers (1), and by the day when it appears in brightness (2), and by Him who created the male and the female (3), indeed your effort is diverse (4). As for him who gives and fears Allah (5), and affirms the best (6), We will ease him toward ease (7). But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient (8), and denies the best (9), We will ease him toward hardship (10).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, swearing by the night when it covers the day with its darkness, extinguishing its light and bringing its gloom: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ the day ﴿and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾. This is also an oath: He swears by the day when it shines, gives light, and becomes visible to the eyes, after the darkness of night had come between them and seeing it directly. Qatadah held that when Allah swears by things, He only swears by them because of their great standing with Him.

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the night when it covers and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾: "Two great signs which Allah folds over the creatures."

* *

As for His words ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾:

This may bear the two meanings I described in His words ﴿by the heaven and He who built it﴾ and ﴿by the earth and He who spread it out﴾. Namely, one may take "mā" to mean "man" (who), so that it is an oath by the Creator of the male and the female, namely that Creator Himself; or one may take "mā" together with what follows it to mean a verbal noun (maṣdar), so that it is an oath by His creating the male and the female.

It has been reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda' that they used to recite it as ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾ (and the male and the female). Abu al-Darda' transmitted this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: In the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): ﴿and the night when it covers, and the day when it appears in brightness, and the male and the female﴾.
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik [[That is, a poor statement. See above p. 165, no. 1.]], who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, who said: Al-Mughirah informed me, who said: I heard Ibrahim say: Alqamah came to Syria and sat down with Abu al-Darda'. He said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "These people kept at it until they nearly led me astray, yet I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Hatim ibn Wardan, who said: Narrated to us Abu Hamzah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: We came to Syria, and I entered upon Abu al-Darda'. He questioned me and said: "How did you hear Ibn Mas'ud recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "That is enough. I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting it thus."
- Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Ulayyah; and Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti narrated to me, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, who said: I arrived in Syria and met Abu al-Darda', who said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Iraq." He said: "From which part?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "Do you recite it in the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Recite ﴿and the night when it covers﴾." So I recited: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾. He laughed, then said: "That is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to me Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to me Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording.
- Narrated to me Abu al-Sa'ib, who said: Narrated to us Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: I came to Syria, and Abu al-Darda' came and said: "Is there anyone among you who can recite to me in the recitation of Abdullah?" They pointed to me. I said: "I can." He said: "How did you hear Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾?" I said: "That is how I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." He said: "These people want me to recite ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾, but I will not follow them."
- Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾. He said: "In some readings it is ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, the same.
- Narrated to me Ahmad ibn Yusuf, who said: Narrated to us al-Qasim, who said: Narrated to us Hajjaj, from Harun, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan, that he used to recite it ﴿wa-mā khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā﴾, saying: "Wa-lladhī khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā" (and He who created the male and the female). Harun said: Abu Amr said: "The people of Mecca say to thunder: 'Glory be to what you glorify.'"
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Jarir, from Mughirah, from Miqsam al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Abi Imran, from Alqamah ibn Qays Abu Shibl: that he came to Syria, entered the mosque, prayed in it, then went to a circle and sat in it. He said: "A man came to me. I recognized in him the way the people gave way to him and stood in awe of him. He sat beside me, so I said: 'Praise be to Allah, I truly hope that Allah has answered my supplication.' That man was Abu al-Darda'. He said: 'What is that?' Alqamah said: 'I asked Allah to grant me a righteous companion, and I hope that you are he.' He said: 'Where are you from?' I said: 'From Kufa,' or 'from the people of Iraq, from Kufa.' Abu al-Darda' said: 'Was there not among you the owner of the two sandals, the cushion and the water vessel,' meaning Ibn Mas'ud? 'Or was there not among you one whom Allah protected from the accursed Satan through the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ),' meaning Ammar ibn Yasir? 'Or was there not among you the keeper of the secret which no one else knows,' or someone other than him, meaning Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman?' Then he said: 'Which of you can memorize as Abdullah used to recite?' I said: 'I can.' He said: 'Recite: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾.' Alqamah said: So I recited ﴿al-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾. Abu al-Darda' said: 'By Him besides whom there is no god, this is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to me, from his mouth to mine.' These people kept at it until they nearly made me give it up."

* *

As for His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾:

He says: Indeed your deeds are diverse, O people, for among you is the unbeliever in his Lord, the one who disobeys Him in His commands and prohibitions, and the believer in Him, the one who obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions.

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾: "It means: different."

* *

As for His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾:

This is the answer to the oath. The meaning is: "By the night when it covers, indeed your effort is diverse." The scholars also said so.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: "The oath concludes here with ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿As for him who gives﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for him who gives and fears Allah among you, O people, in the way of Allah, and whom Allah has commanded to give from his wealth, and what He has bestowed upon him of His bounty, and fears Allah and avoids His prohibitions.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Amir, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾: "He gives what he has and fears Allah." He said: "He fears his Lord."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿As for him who gives﴾ from the bounty ﴿and fears﴾: "He fears his Lord."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿As for him who gives﴾: "the right of Allah," ﴿and fears﴾: "the prohibitions of Allah which He forbade."
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Narrated to us Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾: "He is the one who remembers Allah and fears Allah."

The exegetes differed about the interpretation of His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "and affirms the replacement from Allah for what he gave from his wealth in the matters in which Allah commanded him to give."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to me Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "and affirms the replacement from Allah."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to me Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "He affirms the replacement from Allah."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Ulayyah, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, the same.
- Narrated to us Isma'il ibn Musa al-Suddi, who said: Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-Ahmasi informed us, from Sa'id ibn al-Salt, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "He is certain of the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "that Allah will replace it for him."
- He said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Abu Hashim al-Makki, from Mujahid: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "with the replacement."
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, who said: "with the replacement."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "and affirms that Allah is One, with no partner."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali al-Muqaddami, who said: Narrated to us Ash'ath al-Sijistani, who said: Narrated to us Mis'ar; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Mis'ar, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "There is no god but Allah."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, the same.
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, the same.
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Narrated to us Ubayd, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "There is no god but Allah."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: Narrated to me my father, who said: Narrated to me my paternal uncle, who said: Narrated to me my father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "He affirms 'There is no god but Allah.'"

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "and affirms Paradise."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Mihran, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and affirms the best﴾, he said: "Paradise."
- Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Muhabbab, who said: Narrated to us Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Narrated to us Waki', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "and affirms the promise of Allah."

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "the promise of Allah for Himself, so he acts on that promise which Allah promised."
- Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾: "The believer affirms the good promise of Allah."

The sayings most similar to what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates, and most correct in my view, are: the saying of the one who said that it refers to affirming the replacement from Allah for his spending.

I only said that this is the most correct of the sayings because Allah mentioned before it a spender who spent, seeking from his spending a replacement for it. So the most fitting meaning is that what follows it be a report of his affirming the promise of Allah to him of a replacement, since his spending was in the manner that pleases Him. Moreover, a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a manner similar to what we have said has been transmitted.

Mention of the report transmitted to that effect:
- Narrated to me al-Hasan ibn Salamah ibn Abi Kabshah, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said: Narrated to us Abbad ibn Rashid, from Qatadah, who said: Khulayd al-Asri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no day on which the sun sets but that two angels stand beside it, calling out, which all of Allah's creatures hear except the two jinn and humans: 'O Allah, give the spender a replacement, and give the withholder destruction.'" So Allah revealed in that regard the Qur'an: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best﴾ ... to His words ﴿toward hardship﴾.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to me Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq used to free slaves for Islam in Mecca. He would free old women and women when they embraced Islam. His father said to him: "My son, I see you freeing weak people. If only you freed strong men who would stand with you, protect you, and defend you." He said: "My father, I only want what is with Allah." He said: "One of my household told me that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿As for him who gives and fears and affirms the best, We will ease him toward ease﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾:

He says: We will prepare him for the easy path, which is acting in the way that Allah is pleased with in this world, so that by it He will make Paradise necessary for him in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for him who withholds spending in the way of Allah and refrains from what Allah has bestowed upon him of His bounty, not spending it in the ways Allah commanded, and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord, so that he does not desire to Him by working in His obedience and increasing what He has entrusted to him of that.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with what he has and considers himself self-sufficient within himself."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "and as for him who is stingy with the bounty and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."
- Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: Narrated to me my father, who said: Narrated to me my paternal uncle, who said: Narrated to me my father, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: "He whom Allah has made wealthy, yet he withholds the zakat."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾: "He is stingy with the right of Allah over him and considers himself self-sufficient of his Lord."

As for His words ﴿and denies the best﴾, the exegetes differed about its interpretation, similar to their difference regarding His words ﴿and affirms the best﴾. As for us, we say: its meaning is: "and denies the replacement."

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Humayd ibn Mas'adah, who said: Narrated to us Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, who said: Narrated to us Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "and denies the replacement."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Abd al-Rahman, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and denies the best﴾: "with the replacement from Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies the promise of Allah that He made." Allah said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And the disbeliever denies Allah's good promise."

Others said: Its meaning is: "And denies the oneness of Allah" (tawhid, the affirmation of God's unity).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "And denies: There is no god but Allah."

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾: "There is no god but Allah."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And denies Paradise."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾, he said: "[It means] Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾:

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "We will prepare him in this world for the hard state." It derives from their saying: qad yasarat ghanam fulan (the sheep of so-and-so have "become easy"), meaning when they gave birth and were prepared for birthing. As the poet said:

They claim to be our lords, but they only rule over us
Because their two flocks gave birth with ease.

[The verb irtafa'a al-amr (ارتفع الأمر) means: it ceased and went away, as if it had been placed present and then lifted. From it: irtafa'a al-khilaf baynahuma (the dispute between them was removed).]

It was also said: ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ is not an ease in hardship, because of what came earlier in the beginning of the passage in His words ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾. When two statements are combined, one mentioning good and the other mentioning evil, it is permissible for ease to apply to both together. The "hardship" that Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed us He will ease him toward is: doing what He dislikes and does not approve of.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agrees with what we have said about this.

Mention of the report with that:

⁕ Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he scratched the ground, then raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and his seat in the Fire have been written." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy [for what he was created for]." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Za'ida ibn Qudama narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: We were at a funeral in al-Baqi', when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us and sat, and we sat with him. He had a stick with which he scratched the ground, then he raised his head to the sky and said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that its entrance has been written." The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on our Book? Whoever is among the people of happiness will act for happiness, and whoever is among the people of misery will act for misery." He said: "Rather, act, for each is made easy; as for he who is of the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the works of happiness, and as for he who is of the people of misery, he will be made easy for misery." Then he recited: (﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾).

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, that they both heard Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was at a funeral, took a stick, and began scratching the ground. He said: "There is none but that his seat in the Fire or in Paradise has been written." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy. ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), when he took something from the ground with his hand and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise and in the Fire is known." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, shall we not rely on that?" He said: "No, act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah]﴾ ... the two verses.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Samura ibn Abi Za'ida, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabra, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is none of you, of any soul created, but that Allah has written for it what it will encounter." A Bedouin was with the Prophet (ﷺ), seeking [guidance], and the Bedouin said: "Then what brought me, to strike from the valley of such-and-such, if the matter has already been finished?"

So the Prophet (ﷺ) scratched the ground until the people thought he wished he had not spoken any of it. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Each is made easy for what he was created for. Whoever Allah wishes good for, He makes easy for the path of good, and whoever He wishes evil for, He makes easy for the path of evil." I met Amr ibn Murra and presented this hadith to him, and he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said [it]," and he added in it: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ubayda, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created by [divine] decree﴾, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of action? Is it in something we will begin, or in something that has already been finished?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Act, for each is made easy: We will ease him toward ease, and We will ease him toward hardship."

⁕ Amr ibn Abd al-Malik al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayda narrated to us, saying: al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artat, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who raised the report to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting one day with a stick in his hand, scratching the ground with it. He raised his head and said: "There is none of you but that his seat in Paradise or in the Fire is known." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely [on that]?" He said to them: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." Then he said: "Have you not heard Allah in His Book saying: ﴿As for he who gives and fears [Allah], and believes in the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾?"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾: "[It means] toward evil from Allah."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act for a matter that has been finished, or for a matter we are beginning?" He (ﷺ) said: "Every doer is made easy for his deed."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Talq ibn Habib, from Bashir ibn Ka'b, who said: Two young men asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we act in accordance with what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon, or in something that is being newly begun?" He said: "Rather, in what the pens have dried up over and the decrees have run upon." They said: "Then what is the point of action?" He said: "Act, for each doer is made easy for the deed for which he was created." They said: "Then now we will strive and act."

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 92, verses 1–10 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, may His majesty be exalted and His names be sanctified: ﴿By the night when it covers (1), and by the day when it appears in brightness (2), and by Him who created the male and the female (3), indeed your effort is diverse (4). As for him who gives and fears Allah (5), and affirms the best (6), We will ease him toward ease (7). But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient (8), and denies the best (9), We will ease him toward hardship (10).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, swearing by the night when it covers the day with its darkness, extinguishing its light and bringing its gloom: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ the day ﴿and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾. This is also an oath: He swears by the day when it shines, gives light, and becomes visible to the eyes, after the darkness of night had come between them and seeing it directly. Qatadah held that when Allah swears by things, He only swears by them because of their great standing with Him.

As it is related:
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿By the night when it covers and by the day when it appears in brightness﴾: "Two great signs which Allah folds over the creatures."

* *

As for His words ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾:

This may bear the two meanings I described in His words ﴿by the heaven and He who built it﴾ and ﴿by the earth and He who spread it out﴾. Namely, one may take "mā" to mean "man" (who), so that it is an oath by the Creator of the male and the female, namely that Creator Himself; or one may take "mā" together with what follows it to mean a verbal noun (maṣdar), so that it is an oath by His creating the male and the female.

It has been reported from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda' that they used to recite it as ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾ (and the male and the female). Abu al-Darda' transmitted this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of the report to that effect:
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: In the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): ﴿and the night when it covers, and the day when it appears in brightness, and the male and the female﴾.
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to us Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik [[That is, a poor statement. See above p. 165, no. 1.]], who said: Narrated to us Shu'bah, who said: Al-Mughirah informed me, who said: I heard Ibrahim say: Alqamah came to Syria and sat down with Abu al-Darda'. He said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "How did Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "These people kept at it until they nearly led me astray, yet I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Hatim ibn Wardan, who said: Narrated to us Abu Hamzah, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: We came to Syria, and I entered upon Abu al-Darda'. He questioned me and said: "How did you hear Ibn Mas'ud recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾?" I said: "﴿and the male and the female﴾." He said: "That is enough. I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting it thus."
- Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Ulayyah; and Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti narrated to me, who said: Narrated to us Khalid ibn Abdullah, from Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, who said: I arrived in Syria and met Abu al-Darda', who said: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Iraq." He said: "From which part?" I said: "From the people of Kufa." He said: "Do you recite it in the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Recite ﴿and the night when it covers﴾." So I recited: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾. He laughed, then said: "That is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."
- Narrated to us Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Narrated to me Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to me Dawud, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar wording.
- Narrated to me Abu al-Sa'ib, who said: Narrated to us Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: I came to Syria, and Abu al-Darda' came and said: "Is there anyone among you who can recite to me in the recitation of Abdullah?" They pointed to me. I said: "I can." He said: "How did you hear Abdullah recite this verse: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness and the male and the female﴾?" I said: "That is how I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it." He said: "These people want me to recite ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾, but I will not follow them."
- Narrated to us Ibn Abd al-A'la, who said: Narrated to us Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and by Him who created the male and the female﴾. He said: "In some readings it is ﴿wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾."
- Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Narrated to us Yazid, who said: Narrated to us Sa'id, from Qatadah, the same.
- Narrated to me Ahmad ibn Yusuf, who said: Narrated to us al-Qasim, who said: Narrated to us Hajjaj, from Harun, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan, that he used to recite it ﴿wa-mā khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā﴾, saying: "Wa-lladhī khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā" (and He who created the male and the female). Harun said: Abu Amr said: "The people of Mecca say to thunder: 'Glory be to what you glorify.'"
- Narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Narrated to us Jarir, from Mughirah, from Miqsam al-Dabbi, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Abi Imran, from Alqamah ibn Qays Abu Shibl: that he came to Syria, entered the mosque, prayed in it, then went to a circle and sat in it. He said: "A man came to me. I recognized in him the way the people gave way to him and stood in awe of him. He sat beside me, so I said: 'Praise be to Allah, I truly hope that Allah has answered my supplication.' That man was Abu al-Darda'. He said: 'What is that?' Alqamah said: 'I asked Allah to grant me a righteous companion, and I hope that you are he.' He said: 'Where are you from?' I said: 'From Kufa,' or 'from the people of Iraq, from Kufa.' Abu al-Darda' said: 'Was there not among you the owner of the two sandals, the cushion and the water vessel,' meaning Ibn Mas'ud? 'Or was there not among you one whom Allah protected from the accursed Satan through the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ),' meaning Ammar ibn Yasir? 'Or was there not among you the keeper of the secret which no one else knows,' or someone other than him, meaning Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman?' Then he said: 'Which of you can memorize as Abdullah used to recite?' I said: 'I can.' He said: 'Recite: ﴿and the night when it covers and the day when it appears in brightness﴾.' Alqamah said: So I recited ﴿al-dhakari wa-l-unthā﴾. Abu al-Darda' said: 'By Him besides whom there is no god, this is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to me, from his mouth to mine.' These people kept at it until they nearly made me give it up."

* *

As for His words ﴿indeed your effort is diverse﴾:
